**Voica v0.9.2 — AI term correction survives every way Groq withdraws or refuses a model.**

This release closes out a full check of how AI term correction picks its model, done against the
cross-platform spec and the macOS app — everything it found is here at once.

### A withdrawn model that answers differently

Groq does not report withdrawn models one way. Most answer `404`, but some — `gemma2-9b-it`,
`mixtral-8x7b-32768` — answer `400` with the code `model_decommissioned`. Voica only recognised the
first, so if you had once picked such a model by hand, **term correction silently did nothing on
every dictation** until you opened Settings.

Both are now treated the same: the choice goes back to "Recommended", the dictation is retried once
on a working model, and the next one goes straight there. The answer is recognised by its error code,
not its wording.

### Settings stops crying wolf

With "Recommended" selected, any change of the automatically picked model showed an orange
"Selected model was unavailable — switched to …". The most common case was a good one: you enabled the
better model in the Groq console, and Settings greeted its return with a warning. That message now
appears only when a model **you** picked is gone.

### Nothing refused twice

If a dictation ran out of its 20-second budget while Voica was still finding the next working model,
the search was abandoned — and the next dictation paid for the same refusal again. Now it finishes in
the background, and so does a retry that is refused as well.

### Install

Windows 10 1809+ / x64:

| File | Size | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| **`Voica-Setup-0.9.2.exe`** | ~75 MB | nothing — recommended |
| `Voica.exe` | ~80 MB | nothing — single file, no installation |
| `Voica-fx.exe` | ~37 MB | [.NET 8 Desktop Runtime](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0) installed once |

Installing over an existing copy keeps your history, settings and API key.

Not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn → **More info → Run anyway**
([why, and how to verify](https://github.com/Inhum/voica-win#why-does-windows-warn-about-this-app)).

Full changelog: https://github.com/Inhum/voica-win/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
